source: MAFF Department of Agricultural Extension / ASPIRE Project, IFAD-funded - "ដំណាំក្រូចថ្លុង" (Pomelo Cultivation Guide), 2017, 90pp
text:
Citrus aphids (Toxoptera aurantii and Toxoptera citricidus, family Aphididae) are small sap-sucking insects that cluster on new shoots, young leaves, and flower buds. Heavy infestation causes new growth to curl and distort, weakens the tree, and - because aphids excrete sticky honeydew - promotes sooty mold growth on leaves, which further reduces photosynthesis.

Toxoptera citricidus is of particular concern because it is an efficient vector of citrus tristeza virus ("Tristaza"), a serious disease that can severely stunt or kill infected trees; controlling this aphid is therefore also part of managing virus spread in an orchard.

Aphid populations are often kept in check naturally by predators such as ladybird beetles and by parasitic wasps, so the source recommends monitoring new flushes and only treating with insecticide when aphid numbers are clearly building up and natural enemies are not keeping pace, rather than spraying preventively.
